title: Cold Veggie Pizza Snacks
description: Who doesn’t love cold pizza? DaVita dietitian Vallery created a quick, kidney-friendly pizza that includes five fresh vegetables. Grab a piece for a quick snack or serve at your next social event.
steps: Preheat oven to 350º F. Spray a 13” x 9” x 2” baking pan with nonstick cooking spray.
Roll out crescent rolls onto the baking pan, forming into a single flat dough surface, pressing seams together. Bake 10 to 15 minutes. Let stand until cool, 10 to 15 minutes.
In a bowl, beat cream cheese and sour cream until smooth. Stir in the ranch dressing and garlic powder. Spread the mixture evenly over the crust.
Chop broccoli, carrot, cucumber and onion. Slice cherry tomatoes in half.
Arrange chopped vegetables on top of cream cheese mixture.
Cover pizza with plastic wrap and refrigerate until serving time. Slice 4 even vertical cuts and 5 horizontal cuts for 20 pieces.
hints: Make ahead and eat as a quick snack or serve as an appetizer at your next social event.
For a lower sodium snack substitute the DaVita recipe Easy Pizza Dough for crescent dough.

title: Green Bean Casserole
description: Green Bean Casserole is a long-time holiday favorite. Try a few adjustments recommended by DaVita dietitian Erica to serve up a tasty, healthier version for today’s kidney diet.
steps: Preheat oven to 350° F. Spray a 2-1/2 quart casserole dish with cooking spray.
Crush 10 crackers to equal about 1/2-cup cracker crumbs and set aside.
In a medium skillet, melt 2 tablespoons of butter over medium heat. Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in sugar, sour cream and finely shredded sharp cheddar cheese.
Add the frozen green beans and stir to coat.
Transfer mixture to a prepared casserole dish.
In a small microwave-safe bowl melt 1-tablespoon butter in microwave. Stir in cracker crumbs and sprinkle over top of casserole.
Bake the casserole for 30 minutes or until topping is golden brown.
hints: Remember to take your phosphorus binder with this casserole since it contains cheese, a source of phosphorus.
This recipe is tastier and healthier than the cream soup version of holiday green bean casserole. It is much lower in sodium.

title: Great Way to Start Your Day Bagel
description: Wake up to a Great-Way-to-Start-Your-Day Bagel with tasty tomato and onion sliced on top of a bagel seasoned with lemon pepper. Come to think of it, this delicious, easy to make treat is not just for breakfast but anytime it calls for a great, kidney-friendly dish.
steps: Slice bagel and toast until golden brown.
Spread cream cheese over each bagel half. Place onion slice and tomato slice on top and sprinkle with lemon pepper.
hints: For variety try different types of bagels and flavored cream cheese.
Some brands of lemon pepper contain salt. Check the ingredients and select a brand without salt.

title: Hawaiian Rice
description: Say "aloha" to the kidney-friendly recipe for Hawaiian Rice.
ingredients: 1/2 cup canned pineapple tidbits, in unsweetened juice
steps: Slice mushrooms, chop bell peppers and mince ginger root.
Spray a nonstick frying pan with cooking spray. Sauté mushrooms, bean sprouts, and bell pepper.
Add pineapple, soy sauce, ginger root and salt. Stir and heat thoroughly.
Mix into hot rice and serve.
hints: For a one-dish meal add shrimp or chicken.
1 cup uncooked rice yields 2 cups cooked rice.

title: Barbecue Seasoning Blend
description: Make this seasoning blend for your barbecue. It’s great as a dry rub, or add oil, vinegar or lemon juice to use as a marinade
steps: Mix ingredients together in a jar and shake to combine.
Use as a dry rub or combine with oil, vinegar, lemon juice or other seasonings to make a marinade or sauce.
hints: Adjust the amount used according to taste.

title: Carrot and Jicama Salad
description: Jicama is a root vegetable and it’s loaded with Vitamin C, has low sodium, no fat, and it’s kidney-friendly. It’s deliciously crunchy, somewhat like the Chinese water chestnut. Are you starting to warm up to jicama? Good! Because Betty from California has a terrific Carrot & Jicama Salad that really takes care of that urge to crunch on something.
steps: Grate the carrots and jicama. Chop the cilantro. Combine in a medium bowl.
In a small jar or bowl combine lime juice, oil and honey. Pour over the carrot mixture and toss to combine.
hints: Leftover salad keeps chilled for 2-3 days. Season with pepper or ground cumin if desired.

title: Veggie Crumbles Pita Pizza
description: For a higher protein vegetarian pizza with a beefy taste add seasoned veggie crumbles to a pita pizza. Veggie Crumbles Pita Pizza delivers 18 grams of protein and a full serving of vegetables. If you prefer thin crust, no problem. Simply spit a pita into 2 rounds and proceed as directed.
steps: Preheat the oven to 400 F.
Chop the onion, bell pepper and mushrooms.
In a small nonstick skillet heat the vegetarian crumbles with 2 tablespoons water and the Italian seasoning blend until hot and most of the water is evaporated.
Brush the bottom side or each pita with olive oil, then spread 1-1/2 tablespoons of pizza sauce on each pita.
Distribute the vegetables and vegetarian crumble evenly over both pitas.
Top each pita pizza with 1/4 cup of mozzarella cheese. Bake for 6-8 minutes until cheese is melted.
hints: Check labels on pitas and pizza sauce and select the lowest sodium brands.
Frozen vegetarian crumbles are a soy product that can be used as a replacement for ground beef. If desired you can substitute lean ground beef or turkey.
For a thin crust pizza open the pita and split into 2 round pieces. Carbohydrate is reduced to 22 grams.

title: Mixed Berry Protein Smoothie
description: It’s like dessert in a glass, or a creamy, dreamy drink that doubles as a snack. It’s a kidney-friendly recipe for Mixed Berry Protein Smoothie by DaVita renal dietitian, Cynthia from Utah. Berries have made it big on the health scene because of the vitamins and antioxidants they contain that feed our bodies with lots of health-promoting elements. Cynthia’s smoothie not only has berries, it also has good-for-you protein.
ingredients: 1 cup fresh or frozen mixed berries
1 teaspoon Crystal Light® liquid flavor enhancer drops, any berry flavor
steps: In a blender add water, frozen berries, ice cubes and liquid flavor enhancer drops. Blend until slushy and mixed well.
Add whipped topping and blend well.
Add protein powder. Blend well.
Divide into 2 servings and enjoy one right away or freeze and defrost to enjoy later.
hints: Increase protein powder for a higher protein drink.
Select a combination of your favorite berries: raspberries, strawberries, blueberries or blackberries.

title: Cornbread Muffins with Rice Milk
description: DaVita renal dietitian Jackie from North Carolina has put her own spin on Corn Bread Muffins with a recipe that offers just a hint of sweetness, thanks to the secret ingredients of rice milk, which is a recommended low-phosphorus substitute for milk. This renal-friendly muffin recipe is so easy to make, you can whip up a batch in no time.
ingredients: 1 cup plain cornmeal, white or yellow
2 tablespoon unsalted butter, melted or 2 tablespoons canola oil
steps: Preheat oven to 400° F.
In a bowl, combine flour, cornmeal, sugar and baking powder.
In another bowl, combine egg substitute, rice milk and melted butter.
Stir dry ingredients into wet ingredients just until moistened.
Fill greased or paper-lined muffin cups 2/3 full.
Bake for 15 to 20 minutes or until a toothpick comes out clean.
Serve warm.
hints: By using egg substitute instead of egg and rice milk instead of milk, phosphorus is reduced from 130 mg to 100 mg. The baking powder contributes 76 mg phosphorus to each muffin. Limit portion to one muffin.
Do not substitute self-rising corn meal — it’s higher in phosphorus.
Freeze leftover muffins and reheat for a quick meal addition later.
To make skillet-baked cornbread instead of muffins use a medium-size iron skillet and decrease sugar to 2 tablespoons.

title: Hearty Breakfast Burritos with Pineapple Jalapeno Salsa
description: A recipe that fills the bill for kidney-friendly is Hearty Breakfast Burritos with Pineapple Jalapeno Salsa. Not only does it have fresh fruit and veggies, but you can add a little or a lot of heat by controlling the amount of jalapeno peppers.
ingredients: 2 cups fresh pineapple, cut into 1/2”-inch cubes
1 cup shitake or button mushrooms, sliced and chopped roughly
steps: Prepare salsa first by mixing together pineapple, cilantro, jalapenos, lime juice and brown sugar in a non-reactive bowl (glass, plastic or ceramic). Set aside.
In a nonstick skillet, heat oil and sauté green peppers and mushrooms over medium heat for 2 to 4 minutes.
Drain off excess liquid.
Pour beaten eggs over mixture in skillet and sprinkle the green onion evenly over eggs. As the eggs begin to set pull them across the skillet with a spatula, forming large curds.
Continue cooking and folding eggs until no visible liquid egg remains.
Season with pepper.
Spoon egg mixture onto individual tortillas, divided evenly.
Spoon 1/3 cup pineapple salsa onto each tortilla, fold ends, and roll up burrito-style.
hints: For hotter jalapeno flavor, leave seeds in. For less heat cut down to 1 pepper.
Substitute fresh pineapple with canned pineapple tidbits or chunks.

title: Curried Chicken Thighs
description: Curried Chicken Thighs includes 7 spices plus apple and carrot for natural sweetness. A recipe bonus–you can make extra seasoning mix to use in other curry recipes.
steps: Season both sides of chicken with salt. Mix remaining spices together and season all sides chicken with 1/2 of the seasoning mix. Set chicken aside in the refrigerator for a few hours.
Core and cube the apple; thinly slice carrot diagonally; chop onion and garlic.
Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in the skillet. Add apple, carrots, onion, garlic and remaining spice blend. Reduce heat to medium and sauté until soft, about 10 minutes. Remove from skillet.
In the same skillet, heat the remaining olive oil and add chicken. Turn heat to medium and brown chicken on both sides. Add water and cook uncovered, until water has reduced to at least half.
Add vegetables and cook on low about 10 minutes, until chicken is done.
hints: Serve over rice or cauliflower rice.
Make an extra batch of the seasoning mixture and store in a jar for the next time you make Curried Chicken Thighs.
Replace chicken with shrimp for variety.

title: Asian Soup Jar
description: Assemble low-sodium Asian Soup Jar and refrigerate until ready to eat. Simply add hot water and steep for 2 minutes, then enjoy!
ingredients: 1/2 cup cooked brown or white rice
1/2 cup frozen broccoli, cauliflower and carrots
crushed red pepper flakes to taste (optional)
steps: Place the egg in a pan of water and heat to a boil. Turn heat off and leave egg in water for 8 minutes. Drain water and add cold water to cool the egg.
Layer rice and vegetables in a 16 ounce glass jar.
In a small bowl mix coconut aminos, sesame oil, ginger, garlic powder and red pepper flakes. Pour over rice and vegetables. Top with a lid and refrigerate.
Remove jar from refrigerator at least 15 minutes before you are ready to eat.
Pour 5 ounces boiling water into the jar, close the lid and shake to combine. Let ingredients steep in unopened jar for 2 minutes.
Peel and slice the hard-boiled egg. Pour contents from jar into a bowl, top with egg and enjoy!
hints: Coconut aminos are a lower sodium, gluten-free alternative to soy sauce. One teaspoon has 90 mg sodium compared to 305 mg sodium in one teaspoon soy sauce.
Use the bagged coleslaw mix instead of buying a cabbage and carrot.
Recipe analysis includes brown rice. Substitute rice noodles for rice if desired.
If you use a wide-mouth jar you can mix and eat the soup directly from the jar—no bowl needed.
Double or triple the recipe and refrigerate extra jars for a quick meal.

title: Hula Meatballs
description: Say aloha to Hula Meatballs, a kidney-friendly recipe that is great for parties.
steps: Preheat oven to 375° F.
Grate onion and dice bell peppers.
Combine ground beef, eggs, 1 tablespoon cornstarch, onion, black pepper, nutmeg and garlic powder. Mix well.
Form into 1” balls and place on a baking sheet.
Bake for 10 to 15 minutes, until meatballs are cooked through.
Drain juice from pineapple cans into a measuring cup. Add water to make 2 cups. Reserve pineapple chunks.

Combine remaining 6 tablespoons cornstarch, reduced sodium soy sauce, vinegar, water, unpacked brown sugar, white sugar and pineapple juice. Heat until thickened, stirring constantly. Remove from heat.
Place meatballs, sauce, pineapple chunks, green and red peppers in a covered warming dish or crock pot set on low setting until ready to serve.
hints: Reduced sodium soy sauce contains 500 to 600 mg sodium per tablespoon compared to 950 to 1050 mg sodium in regular soy sauce. Limit to the amount specified in the recipe.
Make meatballs ahead and refrigerate. When ready to serve, heat ingredients together and transfer to a warming dish.

title: Mango Chutney
description: DaVita dietitian Sara serves up a delicious and kidney-friendly recipe for Mango Chutney. Use it on your meat, poultry, fish and even as a salsa for chips.
steps: Finely chop onion. Mince ginger root and garlic.Cut mango into chunks.
In a medium skillet heat oil and sauté onion until soft. Add ginger and garlic; cook for 2 minutes.
Add mango, sugar, vinegar, raisins, cranberries, pepper flakes and allspice.
Bring mixture to a boil then reduce heat to medium. Continue cooking and stirring 10 to 15 minutes until fruit is soft and mixture is thickened.
Refrigerate to chill. Serve with fish, poultry or meat.
hints: Use frozen mango when fresh is not in season.
Adjust chili flakes to your preference.

title: Mexican Chicken Pizza
description: Monterey Jack cheese, onions and red pepper are just some of the enticing ingredients for the kidney-friendly recipe for Mexican Chicken Pizza.
ingredients: 1 cup canned, no salt-added whole-kernel corn
steps: Preheat oven to 350° F.
Place flour tortillas on a baking sheet coated with nonstick cooking spray. Bake at 350° F for 10 minutes or until edges are light brown. Remove from oven; stack and press down to flatten. Set aside.
Drain corn; dice onion, red peppers and chicken. Chop garlic and cilantro.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat; coat pan with cooking spray.
Add corn to skillet and cook 1 minute or until lightly charred. Add onion, red peppers, chicken and garlic; cook 2 minutes or until thoroughly heated.
Remove from heat; stir in lime juice.
Place tortillas on baking sheet. Spoon 3/4-cup chicken mixture onto each tortilla; top each with 2 tablespoons of cheese. Bake at 350° F for 2 minutes or until the cheese melts.
Remove from oven and sprinkle each pizza with 1 teaspoon cilantro.
hints: Always select natural cheeses instead of processed cheese. Sodium and phosphorus contents are usually lower in natural cheeses.
Stick with the recommended cheese portion (2 tablespoons per pizza—or less) to keep phosphorus in a reasonable range.

title: Carrot Cake Cookies
description: Carrots, oats and raisins add goodness and flavor to Carrot Cake Cookies. For extra sweetness, try DaVita dietitian Jessica’s Cream Cheese Frosting.
steps: Set butter out to soften. Finely grate the carrots.
Line 2 baking sheets with parchment paper.
In a medium bowl mix flour, baking soda, baking powder and cinnamon.
Using a mixer, beat sugar and butter until fluffy. Mix in eggs and vanilla and continue beating to combine.
Add flour mixture to wet mixture and beat until blended.
Stir in rolled oats, raisins and carrots. Cover bowl and chill dough in the refrigerator for 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350° F.
Scoop 1/2 tablespoon size balls of dough onto cookie sheets leaving 1 to 2 inches between cookies.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes or until cookies are lightly browned.
Remove from cookie sheet to cool on a rack.
hints: Top each cookie with a tablespoon of Jessica’s Cream Cheese Frosting for extra sweetness.
Make a double batch to share or take to special events.

title: Hungarian Sour Cherry Soup
description: Try a new take on soup with the kidney-friendly recipe for Hungarian Sour Cherry Soup.
steps: Remove pits from cherries.
Add water to a medium sauce pan together with cherries, sugar and salt. Bring to a boil then simmer at a very low heat for 10 minutes.
Remove 2 tablespoons of liquid and set aside for garnish.
Remove another 1/4 cup of the liquid and allow to cool slightly.
Whisk together with the flour and sour cream then return to the sauce pan.
Simmer for another 5 minutes over low heat.
Remove from heat and allow to cool.
Serve in a soup bowl. Swirl in the reserved cherry juice as a garnish.
hints: Alter the sugar or Splenda to your taste.
If Splenda or other sugar replacement is substituted for sugar the carbohydrate is 16 grams per serving which equals one Carbohydrate Choice.
Look for canned cherries in juice or light syrup to make this an even easier recipe.

This is an excellent light lunch for those who have no taste for meat, fish, poultry, etc. To increase the protein content add protein powder as advised by your renal dietitian. Two scoops of ProSource® or ProCel® protein powder are excellent additions.

title: Grab ‘n’ Go Southwestern Salad
description: Grab a jar and build Jenifer’s Grab ‘n’ Go Southwestern Salad. It’s the perfect recipe for making quick kidney-friendly salads to grab for lunch before dashing out the door.
steps: Mix frozen veggies and lettuce in a bowl. (If eating immediately thaw vegetables before mixing with the lettuce.)
Toss with dressing and divide into 4 servings. Portion into 12 to 16 ounce jars or portable lunch containers.
Add 2 cherry tomatoes to each salad serving.
Seal and refrigerate salad jars until ready to go. Keeps for 3 to 4 days refrigerated.
Divide croutons into 1/4 cup servings and store in small containers or snack bags (do not refrigerate). Add to salad when ready to eat.
hints: Decrease sodium to only 125 mg per serving by using Creamy Vinaigrette Dressing instead of store bought dressing.
Southwestern blend veggies contain corn, green peppers, onions and black beans.
Add cooked chicken or low-sodium canned tuna for added protein.

title: Chicken Vegetable Linguine
description: If you’re a fan of chicken, vegetables and noodles, you’re going to love this kidney-friendly recipe for Chicken Vegetable Linguine. It’s a real treat for your taste buds from DaVita dietitian Beth.
ingredients: 3/4 teaspoon Mrs. Dash® herb seasoning blend
steps: Cut chicken into small strips.
Heat pan on medium heat with 2 tablespoons extra virgin olive oil.
Add chicken to pan and cook until done.
Cook 4 ounces of linguine according to package directions.
Cut broccoli and cauliflower to bite-size pieces.
When chicken is cooked, add broccoli, cauliflower, carrots, tomatoes and lemon juice, cover and cook for 3 minutes.
Add drained pasta to pan and then add 1 tablespoon extra virgin olive oil and stir.
Add Mrs. Dash, stir and simmer on low for 5 minutes.
hints: Use your favorite variety of Mrs. Dash herb seasoning blend.
Store remaining uncooked linguine or cook the whole package and use half in another recipe.

title: Tortilla Rollups
description: Throw a fiesta with Tortilla Rollups for people on a dialysis diet. This kidney-friendly recipe will make your mouthwater.
ingredients: 1 teaspoon Mrs. Dash® original herb seasoning blend
steps: Chop spinach. Dice onion, pimento and turkey breast. Drain pineapple.
Spread cream cheese over each tortilla to cover. Sprinkle with Mrs. Dash® herb seasoning.
Place remaining ingredients in a bowl and mix.
Divide mixed ingredients into 2 portions. Place half on each tortillas and roll up like a jelly roll.
Trim ends and slice each roll into 6 pieces.
hints: Wrap un-cut roll in plastic wrap and refrigerate until ready to cut and serve.
Compare tortilla brands and select the lowest in sodium.

title: Quick Pan-Glazed Chicken
description: Quick Pan-Glazed Chicken is loaded with tasty ingredients like honey, basil and balsamic vinegar that also happen to be powerful antioxidants. Using skinless chicken breasts sautéed in olive oil, this kidney-friendly recipe by Christine, a DaVita dietitian from New Jersey, is high in lean protein and low in saturated fats.
steps: Heat olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Add chicken and sprinkle with pepper.
Sauté chicken for 5 minutes on each side, until brown.
Add balsamic vinegar and sauté for one minute, flipping chicken over to coat.
Add honey and basil. Stir and flip chicken to coat. Cook for one minute longer.
Remove to a plate and spoon pan sauce over chicken.
hints: Be creative and season chicken with herbs or low sodium seasoning blends of your own choice. Garlic and onion powder go well with the black pepper.
If you are on a lower protein diet, decrease the portion to 1/2 chicken breast or substitute smaller boneless chicken thighs for the breast meat.

title: Huevos Rancheros
description: DaVita dietitians, Kara and Maria from Arizona, have put together a regional menu of favorite foods from the Southwest. Here is their recipe for a kidney-friendly version of Huevos Rancheros.
serving_size: 1 tortilla, 1 egg, 1/4 cup red chile sauce
steps: Chop the onion and bell pepper.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a skillet and crisp the tortillas for about a minute on each side or until they start to brown. Set aside on paper towels to drain.
In the same skillet, sauté the onion and bell pepper until soft. (Add additional oil if needed.) Remove from skillet.
Heat remaining oil in the skillet and cook eggs over easy.
Place one crisp tortilla on each plate and top with egg and sautéed vegetables.
Serve with red chile sauce.
hints: Crisp tortillas are available at the grocery store.
To reduce fat in this recipe, crisp the tortillas in the oven and use a nonstick skillet sprayed with cooking spray to prepare eggs.
Make the Chile Colorado Sauce (Basic Red Chili Sauce) recipe on DaVita.com to serve with this recipe.

title: Snack Mix
description: Snack Mix is a tasty, kidney-friendly snack to tide you over. Cereals, pretzels, popcorn and spices make it so delicious. You can also put Snack Mix into your favorite serving dish when you have company over or when you attend a party.
steps: Preheat oven to 350° F.
Mix cereals, pretzels and popcorn in large bowl.
Combine melted margarine, garlic powder and onion powder. Pour over cereal mixture and toss to coat. Add Parmesan cheese.
Bake for 7 to 10 minutes.
Cool before serving.
Store in sealed container.
hints: To reduce sodium further, use unsalted margarine or unsalted butter. Select the rice and corn cereal brand lowest in sodium.
For an added holiday twist, add 1 cup dried cranberries to the snack mix after it has cooled.

title: Fish and Seafood Seasoning
description: Make this seasoning for your fish and seafood meals. DaVita’s recipes are delicious, kidney-friendly, and submitted by DaVita dietitians.
steps: Crush the fennel seeds.
Place ingredients in a jar and shake to combine.
Store until ready to use on fish or seafood.
hints: Use seasoning as a dry rub or mix with oil and lemon juice for a marinade.

title: Lemon Cooler
description: Southwestern cooking from the Arizona region has its own vibrant personality, based on Spanish and Mexican influences. With all those spicy flavors, it’s good to have a tasty and refreshing beverage to wash it all down. DaVita renal dietitian, Elaine from Arizona, offers her kidney-friendly recipe for Lemon Cooler.
steps: Place all ingredients in a blender.
Set on ice/crush setting and blend for 30 seconds to one minute or until ice is well chopped and slush is at desired consistency.
Pour into a glass and garnish with lemon wedge, if desired.
hints: For people with diabetes substitute stevia, Splenda® or other preferred low calorie sweetener for sugar. Calories are reduced to 90 and carbohydrate is 6 grams.
May be used as a calorie booster for those who need extra calories in their diet.
Remember to count this toward your total daily fluid intake if you are on a fluid restriction.

title: Cream Cheesy Burgers
description: DaVita dietitians are great ones for experimentation. And that’s exactly how Cream Cheesy Burgers came about. When DaVita renal dietitian, Judy from Illinois, tried various blends of cream cheese on other sandwiches and liked it, she wondered what it would taste like on this kidney-friendly burger.
steps: Mix ground beef, eggs, basil, onion powder and garlic powder together.
Separate meat into eight 2-ounce patties.
Take 1-1/2 tablespoons of the cream cheese and place on top of a patty.
Take another patty and place it on top, to sandwich the cream cheese between the two patties.
Repeat this procedure with the remaining patties.
Cook in a frying pan or on a grill to desired doneness.
Serve burgers on a bun with lettuce, onion and condiment of choice.
hints: For a variation, combine all the ingredients together with cream cheese in the meat, make four 4-ounce patties and cook.
Top burger with ketchup or steak sauce without the bun for variety.
Recipe may be varied by rolling cream cheese in bread crumbs or panko crumbs.
Patties cook best in a frying pan, in their own juices.
Many herbs and flavorings work well to add flavor without sodium — try using horseradish, oregano or Italian seasoning.
For a lower protein diet make 6 burgers instead of 4 burgers

title: Marinated Fresh Vegetables
description: No cooking is required to create this recipe for Marinated Fresh Vegetables. Just cut up fresh vegetables including broccoli, cauliflower, mushroom, green pepper, celery, onions and mix the marinade. After refrigerating for three hours, you’ll have a cool, kidney-friendly and flavorful side dish.
steps: Cut broccoli and cauliflower into bite-sized pieces. Slice bell peppers and celery. Finely chop onion.
Combine broccoli, cauliflower, mushrooms, bell pepper and celery.
In a separate bowl, combine remaining ingredients to make marinade. Mix well and pour over vegetables. Refrigerate at least 3 hours before serving.
Use a slotted spoon to remove vegetables from marinade before serving.
hints: Adjust portion size to 1/2 cup for a lower potassium serving (167 mg).
Leftovers will keep well in the refrigerator for 5 days.

title: Tuna Veggie Salad
description: The next time you bring a side dish to a party, consider making the delicious, healthy and kidney-friendly Tuna Veggie Salad.
ingredients: 5 ounces canned tuna packed in water
steps: Dice bell peppers and thinly slice zucchini; Chop green onions and basil; mince garlic.
Pour 3/4 cup of water into a medium saucepan.
Place diced bell peppers and sliced zucchini into a steamer basket and place over the saucepan. Heat water to a boil and steam vegetables for 10 minutes.
Remove vegetables from heat, drain off any excess water and transfer to a serving bowl.
Add tuna, green onions and basil. Toss to combine ingredients.
To make dressing, combine vinegar, oil, garlic and black pepper in a jar with a tight-fitting lid and shake well.
Pour dressing over tuna and vegetable mixture and mix well.
hints: Recipe analysis includes low-sodium, canned tuna. If regular canned tuna is used, sodium is 160 mg per serving. Rinse tuna to further reduce sodium.

title: Beef Tibs Lower Protein
description: Beef Tibbs, a popular Ethiopian dish made of spicy beef, is juicy and delicious. In its traditional form, it’s not very kidney-friendly, but DaVita renal dietitian Hanna from Maryland has adapted Beef Tibbs so that people on a kidney diet can enjoy it.
steps: Thinly slice onion. Chop tomato and bell pepper. Cut beef into small cubes.
Sauté onion and oil in a skillet until the onion is slightly brown.
Add beef and tomatoes.
When partially cooked, add bell pepper or jalapeño pepper.
Continue cooking until meat is tender.
Add salt and pepper and serve.
hints: Tibbs is a common Ethiopian dish that can be served with pita bread, half of a piece of injera or 1-cup cooked rice.
Variations of Beef Tibbs can be prepared by adding different ingredients of your choice.
To make dish more spicy, add a chopped jalapeño pepper.

title: Rotini Salad
description: Have fun with the corkscrew shape of rotini pasta when you make this kidney-friendly recipe, Rotini Salad.
steps: Place beaten eggs, 1/2 teaspoon black pepper, dry mustard, salt, prepared mustard, sugar and flour in a saucepan and mix well.
Add water, vinegar and butter. Stir to mix well.
Cook over medium heat; bring to a boil and continue boiling until mixture thickens, stirring constantly.
Cool dressing before adding to rotini mixture.
Cook rotini according to directions on package, omitting the salt.
Drain and rinse with cold water.
Chop onion and eggs; dice cucumber.
In a large bowl, mix rotini, onion, eggs, cucumber and pepper.
Add homemade salad dressing and mix well.
Refrigerate several hours before serving.
hints: Rotini is pasta shaped like little corkscrews.
4 ounces dry rotini yields 2-1/2 cups cooked.
To reduce cholesterol, omit 4 egg yolks from the hard boiled eggs.

title: Chicken and Summer Vegetable Kebabs
description: Here’s a nice summer meal you can make on the grill. Chicken and Summer Vegetable Kebabs feature zucchini, peppers and onions with a tasty glaze. It’s a great kidney-friendly recipe for those warm summer months.
ingredients: 1 teaspoon Mrs. Dash® herb seasoning blend
steps: To make the marinade, measure the peach jam into a small microwave safe bowl and heat for 10 to 15 seconds to liquefy. Add the olive oil, lemon juice, Mrs. Dash® herb seasoning and salt. Stir until well blended.
Rinse the chicken thighs and pat dry with a paper towel. Cut each thigh into 4 pieces and place in a zip-top bag.
Add 3 tablespoons marinade to the chicken pieces. (Reserve 2 tablespoons marinade to use on vegetables.) Seal the zip-top bag and refrigerate to marinate.

Cut the vegetables into even bite-sized pieces for the kebabs (zucchini-8 slices; yellow squash-8 slices; red pepper-16 pieces; onion-varies). Place them in a medium bowl and add reserved marinade. Stir to coat the vegetable pieces.
Thread the vegetables and chicken pieces onto skewers (4 large or 8 small skewers).
Heat the grill to medium heat. Place the skewers on the grill and cook covered for 12 to 15 minutes. Turn the skewers 2 or 3 times to cook evenly.
hints: To prevent the kebabs from sticking to the grill, use tongs to wipe grates with an oily paper towel before placing the kebabs on grill.
For a lower or higher protein diet decrease or increase the amount of chicken.

title: Grilled Buttermilk Garlic Marinated Chicken
description: Four simple ingredients for a marinade and the chicken part of your choice is an easy way to boost flavor while keeping sodium low and additives out. DaVita dietitian Jessica created Grilled Buttermilk Garlic Chicken to share with her dialysis patients for summer grilling. And in case you were wondering, only 25% of the marinade is absorbed so even with the buttermilk this recipe is kidney-friendly.
ingredients: 2 chicken breasts, bone-in, with skin (or 4 chicken drumsticks)
steps: Chop the garlic cloves.
To make the marinade add buttermilk, olive oil, garlic and black pepper to a large zip top bag. Seal the bag and shake to combine ingredients.
Place chicken in the buttermilk marinade, seal bag and shake to distribute evenly.
Refrigerate the chicken at least 2 hours, or up to 24 hours.
Preheat a grill to medium heat. Remove the chicken from marinade and place on the grill. Discard extra marinade. Grill the chicken until internal temperature reaches 160-165º F.
hints: This recipe can be easily adjusted to accommodate more or less chicken. For every one pound of chicken use 1 cup buttermilk and 1 tablespoon oil.
For additional seasoning, add any of your favorite herbs or spices including parsley, rosemary or basil
Approximately 25% of the marinade is absorbed. Recipe analysis based on this rule.
Adjust the portion for a lower or higher protein diet.
If preferred you can substitute boneless, skinless chicken breast or thighs.

title: Corn Tortillas
description: Homemade means you have more control over ingredients. These homemade Corn Tortillas are low in sodium and easy to make with only 4 ingredients and 4 step.
steps: Mix masa, water and salt in a bowl.
Turn mixture onto a board and knead until a soft dough forms, adding more water as needed.

Divide dough into 16 pieces, each about 1/2-inch wide and 1/2-inch thick. Place each piece of dough between two pieces of plastic to prevent sticking, and then flatten into a 5-inch diameter tortilla using a rolling pin or a tortilla press.

Lightly oil a very hot griddle and place one tortilla on it. Cook for about 30 seconds, then turn the tortilla and cook for another 30 seconds before removing from griddle. (It should be soft and easy to fold.) Repeat for each remaining tortilla.
hints: Use a spatula to pick up the tortilla so you don’t get burned.
Masa is corn flour made from ground hominy. It is used to make tortillas and tamales.
Prepare enchiladas, tacos and quesadillas, or eat 1 to 2 tortillas with a meal.

title: Easy Crispy Lemon Chicken
description: Chicken is a great source of quality protein. People on dialysis need quality protein in their diets to help them keep up their albumin levels and stay healthy. But chicken doesn’t have to be boring. DaVita renal dietitian, Dee from Nevada, provides a tasty main dish that makes having chicken a special occasion. Easy Crispy Lemon Chicken is fresh and zesty.
serving_size: 3 ounces chicken plus 2/3 cup cooked rice
ingredients: 1 teaspoon Mrs. Dash® herb seasoning blend
steps: Prepare rice according to package directions, omitting salt.
Cut one lemon into 6 wedges to use as garnish. Cut the other 4 lemons in half.
Cut chicken into finger-like slices; season with Mrs. Dash® herb seasoning, salt and pepper.
In a medium bowl beat the egg and water until combined.
Dip chicken in eggs and then in flour. Make sure you cover both sides with flour.
Heat olive oil in a non-stick frying pan.
Sauté chicken in the pan until golden brown on both sides. If desired, sauté with lemon wedges for flavor and garnish. Be careful not to over cook chicken.
Squeeze the 6 lemon halves onto chicken throughout sautéing.
Right before removing chicken from pan, squeeze last drops of lemon juice onto chicken.
Take chicken out of pan. Blot excess oil from chicken with paper towels to keep it crispy.
Divide chicken into 6 servings and place each serving on top of 2/3 cup of white rice.
Garnish chicken and rice with lemon wedges and fresh parsley.
hints: If desired, omit salt and pepper and increase Mrs. Dash® herb seasoning to 2 teaspoons.
When removing chicken from frying pan, remove any lemon seeds that may have dropped onto the chicken pieces.
If desired, juice the lemon halves and sprinkle the juice over chicken while sautéing.
Use any type of plain white rice. If desired, add an extra tablespoon of parsley to rice after cooking.
Weight of chicken portion includes breading; yield is approximately 2 ounces chicken. Adjust portion to match your meal plan based on your protein needs.

title: Sweet Cherry Cream Pie
description: DaVita dietitian, Kim from Missouri, helps her dialysis patients eat well and stay healthy with plenty of enthusiasm and mouthwatering recipes. Here’s your chance to give one of her kidney-friendly recipes a try. Kim shares her lip-smacking Sweet Cherry Cream Pie.
ingredients: 21 ounces canned or bottled cherry pie filling
steps: Soften cream cheese. In a large bowl, mix cream cheese, sugar and vanilla with a mixer.
For the whipped cream, place bowl and beaters of a hand-mixer in freezer for 10-15 minutes. Remove bowl from freezer, put heavy cream in the bowl and beat until soft peaks form.
Fold whipped cream into cream cheese mixture.
Pour mixture into graham cracker pie crust.
Top with cherry pie filling.
Refrigerate until ready to serve.
hints: Substitute Splenda® No Calorie Sweetener and low-sugar pie filling to reduce calories to 299 and carbohydrate to 29 grams. Count as 2 carbohydrate choices.
For variation, use apple- or peach-pie filling instead of cherry.

title: 3-2-1 Cupcakes
description: Now you can make a single cupcake and it’s as esay as 1-2-3! That’s because DaVita renal dietitian Mary A. from California shares her 3-2-1 Cupcakes recipe and the easy instructions: 3 tablespoons cake mix, 2 tablespoons water and 1 minute in the microwave.
steps: In a large plastic bag with a zip lock, pour in angel food cake mix and lemon (or other flavor) cake mix. With the plastic bag sealed, mix the two dry cake mixes together. Use mix to make a single cupcake or a whole batch by following steps 2 through 6.
Spray a small custard dish with non-stick cooking spray.
Measure 3 tablespoons of the dry cake mix and place into a greased custard dish.
Add 2 tablespoons of water and mix with a small fork.
Place in the microwave and cook on high for one minute.
Slip cupcake out of the custard dish. Cool one minute before enjoying.
hints: *Add 2 tablespoons water for each cupcake.
If desired, may frost with cool whip or a glaze after cupcake is completely cooled.
One of the cake mixes must be angel food cake. Strawberry cake mix can be substituted for lemon.
Store dry cake mix in an air-tight container.
The name 3-2-1 Cupcake indicates 3 tablespoons cake mix, 2 tablespoons water and 1 minute in the microwave.
The baking powder in cake mix adds to sodium and phosphorus content. If you take phosphate binders to help control phosphorus, ask your dietitian if you need to take a binder with a cupcake snack.

title: Apple Cinnamon Maple Granola
description: Apple Cinnamon Maple Granola has you covered for breakfast, a snack, or dessert topping.
steps: Preheat oven to 275° F. Line 2 large baking sheets with parchment paper.
Combine dry ingredients in a large bowl.
Combine wet ingredients in a small bowl.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients bowl. Mix very well to coat dry ingredients.
Divide mixture onto the 2 baking sheets.
Bake for 50 minutes to 1 hour, changing pan position (move pan on top rack to bottom rack) halfway through baking.
hints: Instant oats contain added salt. Old fashioned rolled oats are preferable as they are lower in sodium.
Packaged apple chips vary in size. Select the brand closest to 3.4 ounces.
Store granola in an airtight container. Enjoy with Maple Cinnamon Roasted Pears, unenriched almond or rice milk, cottage cheese or yogurt.
For a gluten-free version be sure to use oats and puffed rice cereal that indicates gluten-free on the label.

title: Roast Lamb
description: Julianna from New York has created a kidney-friendly version of Roast Lamb that is great for a spring celebration or for an everyday high quality protein entree.
ingredients: 1 boneless leg of lamb, well-trimmed, rolled and tied (about 4-1/2 pounds)
2 tablespoons oregano leaves, dried and crushed
steps: Preheat oven to 325° F. Set butter out to bring to room temperature.
Wash and lightly trim the fat from the lamb and set aside in a roasting pan.
Chop rosemary and mince the garlic.
Blend the oregano, rosemary, garlic, salt and pepper and half the soft butter or margarine together in a small bowl.
Make slits into the leg of lamb with a sharp knife and stuff the herb and butter mixture into the slits.
Spread the remaining herb and butter mixture over the lamb.
Mix lemon juice with remaining butter and pour over lamb.
Cover and bake 30 minutes for each pound.
After an hour, remove the lid, add the water to the drippings in the pan and baste often until the meat is well browned and tender.
Uncover during the last half hour of cooking for a crisp skin.
hints: For a lower protein diet reduce portion to match your meal plan or check with the dietitian to determine portion size.

Use this guide for cooking times: medium rare, 145° F internal temperature, 20 to 30 minutes per pound; medium, 160° F internal temperature, 30 to 35 minutes per pound; well done, 170° F internal temperature, 35 to 40 minutes per pound.

title: Cream Cheese Thumbprint Cookies
description: Add extra flavor to homemade cookies, cupcakes or cake with Cream Cheese Frosting. Only four ingredients, and it’s easy to make.
steps: Set cream cheese and butter out to soften.
Whip softened cream cheese until fluffy. Add butter and vanilla extract and mix together.
Gradually add in powdered sugar until frosting is smooth.
hints: Use frosting to frost a cake, cupcakes or cookies or try this frosting with Jessica’s Carrot Cake Cookies.
Frosting will keep for about 5 days in the refrigerator.

title: St. Louis Gooey Butter Cake
description: It’s not a celebration, unless there’s cake. DaVita dietitian Martha from Missouri shares her delicious recipe for St. Louis Gooey Butter Cake, which she has adapted to be kidney friendly. After one bite of this yummy cake, you won’t want to wait for the next celebration to prepare this fabulous dessert.
ingredients: 1/2 cup liquid non-dairy creamer (such as Coffee Rich®)
steps: Preheat oven to 350° F.
In a bowl, mix 1 cup flour and 1/4 cup sugar.
Using a pastry blender, cut in 1/4 cup butter until mixture looks like fine crumbs and starts to cling together.
Pat into the bottom of an ungreased 9 x 9 x 2″ baking pan.
In a large mixing bowl, beat 1-1/4 cups sugar and 3/4 cup butter with electric mixer until combined. Beat in corn syrup and eggs.
Alternately add remaining 1 cup flour and non-dairy creamer, beating on low speed after each addition just until combined. (Batter may look slightly curdled.)
Pour batter over crust, spreading evenly to edges of pan.
Bake for 35 minutes or until nearly firm when shaken.
Cool in pan on wire rack. Sprinkle with powdered sugar when cool.
Cut into 12 squares and serve.
hints: For a special topping, add some berries or other low potassium sliced fruit and a dollop of whipped topping.

title: Gingersnap Cookies
description: Cloves, cinnamon, ginger and molasses are a requirement for perfect Gingersnap Cookies. Why wait for the holidays? Make a batch today.
steps: Sift the flour, baking soda, cloves, ginger and cinnamon together.
Cream softened butter with a mixer until light and fluffy; gradually add sugar.
Blend in the egg and molasses.
Add the flour mixture a small amount at a time, until a dough forms.
Cover and refrigerate dough for 1 hour or overnight.
Preheat oven to 350˚ F.
Form dough into balls (heaping teaspoon size) and place 2-inches apart on a greased cookie sheet, flattening each ball slightly.
Bake for 8 to 10 minutes. Cool on a wire rack. Makes 4 dozen cookies.
hints: Store in a covered container.
Gingersnap Cookies are a yummy kitchen gift during the holidays–or anytime!

title: Grilled Salmon Sandwiches with Chipotle Mayonnaise
description: Salmon is a great source of omega-3 fatty acids, known to reduce inflammation and decrease risk of cancer and heart disease. DaVita dietitian Joseph from Maryland created Grilled Salmon Open Faced Sandwiches with Chipotle Mayonnaise to share healthy meal ideas with his dialysis patients.
steps: Preheat grill to medium-high heat. Rub salmon fillets with 1 tablespoon of the olive oil. Place salmon fillets on the grill and cover. Cook until the flesh flakes easily, 10 to 15 minutes.

In a small bowl, combine remaining olive oil, lime juice and lemon-pepper seasoning."#4. While salmon is resting, brush the sourdough bread with olive oil and place on the grill grates and grill 1-2 minutes on each side, or until toasted.
Remove salmon from grill, and allow to rest, covered with foil on a plate for 5-10 minutes. Remove the skin.
While salmon is resting, place sourdough bread on grill grates and allow 1-2 minutes on each side, or until toasted.
To assemble the open faced sandwich, start with sourdough bread, and top with an even amount of chipotle mayo, then the arugula, salmon, and top with the roasted red peppers.
hints: For a lower protein meal plan divide salmon fillets in half. Protein content is 15 grams per sandwich.
Consider adding diced scallions or chives for garnish.
Be sure there is no added salt in the lemon-pepper seasoning by looking at the ingredient list.
If you don’t like salmon, try using a different fish, such as cod or trout.
Sourdough bread could be substituted with other types of breads.
Chipotle mayonnaise has a slightly spicy/smoky flavor. If you dislike these flavors, easily substitute pesto sauce, plain mayonnaise, or dijonnaise (Dijon mustard and mayonnaise mixed).

title: Café au Lait Protein Wake-Up
description: Everyone loves a cup of Joe in the morning. But now kidney patients can kick-start the day with something even better: Café au Lait Protein Wake-Up, a kidney-friendly hot beverage from renal dietitian Sue in from North Carolina.
steps: Place 1 scoop protein powder in a coffee cup. Add coffee, and stir with a small wire whisk until dissolved.
Add flavored coffee creamer.
hints: Add ice for Iced Café au Lait. Count in fluid allowance if you are limiting liquids.
Add additional sweetener of choice if desired.
Refrigerate leftover morning coffee to easily make this treat any time of the day.
Nutrition information varies with the type of protein powder used. Ask your dietitian for a recommendation of brands acceptable for your diet.

title: Lemonade or Limeade Base
description: Try the tangy kidney-friendly recipe for Lemonade or Limeade Base on your next picnic.
ingredients: 1-1/4 cups sugar or Splenda® sugar substitute
1/2 teaspoon finely shredded lemon or lime peel
1-1/4 cups fresh lemon or lime juice
steps: In a medium saucepan, stir water and sugar or sugar substitute over medium heat until sugar is dissolved. Remove from heat; cool 20 minutes. (If you are in a hurry skip the heat. Instead, dissolve the sugar in room temperature water then go to step #2.)
Add citrus peel and juice to sugar mixture. Pour into a jar or pitcher; cover and chill. Keeps for up to 3 days.

For each glass of lemonade or limeade, combine 3 ounces base and 3 ounces water in ice-filled glasses. Stir and sip slowly to enjoy. Freeze leftover base in ice cube trays and add to beverages instead of ice.
hints: 3 ounces liquid is 6 tablespoons.
Base made with Splenda® instead of sugar has 20 calories and 5 grams carbohydrate. Count as 1/2 carbohydrate choice.

title: High Protein Cookies
description: Amy from Texas took on a problem and turned it into a solution with her recipe for High-Protein Cookies for the dialysis diet. By combining oatmeal, margarine and protein powder, Amy took the cholesterol out and put protein “the body builder of nutrition” in.
ingredients: 1 teaspoon baking powder (if soft cookies are desired)
steps: Preheat oven to 325°F.
In a mixing bowl, beat margarine and brown sugar.
Blend in egg and vanilla.
Combine remaining ingredients. Mix will be very dry. (You can add 1 tablespoon of molasses or water to make it stick together.)
Spray a cookie sheet with non-stick spray.
Roll batter into 1-inch balls, and place on sheet.
Bake for 10 minutes.
hints: Use old fashioned or quick cooking oatmeal. Avoid instant oatmeal because sodium content is much higher.
Omit baking powder for a crunchy cookie. Phosphorus will decrease to 42 mg per serving and sodium decreases to 146 mg.

Soy protein powder may be used but nutrient content will change. Soy protein is usually higher in phosphorus compared to whey protein powder. Ask your dietitian for a list of recommended protein powders that are lowest in phosphorus and potassium.

title: Seasoned Cabbage Steaks
description: Seasoned Cabbage Steaks add a new twist to this high-antioxidant cruciferous vegetable. Only 5 ingredients, and all you have to do is slice, season and bake.
steps: Preheat oven to 350° F.
Cut cabbage head into six 1″ thick slices.
Arrange cabbage slices on a baking sheet and drizzle with olive oil. Sprinkle seasoning blend and dill weed over cabbage. Cover with aluminum foil.
Bake for 45 minutes. Remove foil and let cabbage steaks brown in oven for 15 minutes longer.
hints: Make a sauce with 1/2 cup Greek yogurt and additional chopped fresh dill weed to serve with the cabbage steaks if desired.

title: Purple Punch
description: Put some color in your punch bowl with the kidney-friendly recipe for Purple Punch.
ingredients: 4 six-ounce cans frozen grape juice concentrate, thawed
steps: Combine ginger ale and grape juice concentrate in a large punch bowl.
Scoop sherbet into punch and stir to mix.
hints: Not recommended for persons with diabetes due to high carbohydrate content.

title: Almost Mashed Potatoes
description: Trying to fit foods you love into the dialysis diet can be a challenge. DaVita renal dietitian, Amity in Florida, works with her patients to find foods low in phosphorus, potassium and sodium. Here is a favorite that has been modified for the renal diet — Almost Mashed Potatoes. Enjoy this great taste and still maintain your kidney-friendly diet.
steps: Cut the cauliflower into pieces and rinse with water.
Place the cauliflower pieces in a microwave safe dish, cover and cook on high for 8 to 10 minutes or until soft.
Drain off moisture from the cooked cauliflower.
Carefully place the hot cauliflower in a blender and blend until smooth.
Add the cream cheese, garlic and pepper. Blend to combine ingredients.
Remove mixture from the blender and serve hot.
hints: One medium head cauliflower yields 6 cups.
Garlic powder may be substituted for the minced garlic.
Since cauliflower is bland like potatoes, this recipe tastes similar to mashed potatoes. The potassium content is 100 mg lower per serving.
To reduce fat content, use light cream cheese. Protein, sodium, potassium and phosphorus content will be slightly higher.

title: Creamy Fruit Salad
description: Enjoy kidney-friendly recipe Creamy Fruit Salad by Akemi from Nebraska. Fruits in the recipe can be substituted with any low potassium fruits of your choice, and if low sugar or no sugar is a must, substitute artificial sweetener.
ingredients: 15 ounces canned peaches in light syrup
steps: Cut apples, pears and peaches into bite-size pieces. Cut strawberries into quarters.
Place cut fruit in a large bowl. Set aside.
Place a metal bowl and metal beaters of a hand mixer in the freezer for 15 to 30 minutes. Pour heavy cream into the bowl and mix with chilled beaters until stiff peaks form.
In a medium bowl, mix cream cheese, sugar, and sour cream until smooth. Gently fold in whipped cream until mixed well.
Just before serving, pour cream cheese mixture over fruit and gently stir.
Top with fresh berries and serve.
hints: Substitute with any low potassium fruits of your choice. Make it colorful! (blueberries, raspberries, blackberries or a mixture).
This is my family’s favorite fruit salad recipe and a great potluck item. It’s best to eat it the same day because it can get watery overnight.
Reduce ingredients in half to make a smaller amount.

title: Apple Onion Omelet
description: Try this delicious recipe for Apple Onion Omelet by DaVita dietitian Brenda from Washington. She uses some of her favorite regional foods so you can create a delicious, dialysis-appropriate meal with splendid flavors from the Pacific Northwest.
steps: Preheat oven to 400º F.
Peel and core apple. Thinly slice apple and onion.
Beat eggs with milk, water and pepper in a small bowl; set aside.
Over medium heat, melt butter in a small, ovenproof skillet.
Add onion and apple to the skillet and sauté until onion becomes translucent, about 5 to 6 minutes.
Spread out the onion and apple mixture evenly in the skillet.

Pour egg mixture evenly into the skillet and cook over medium heat until the edges begin to set. Sprinkle the cheddar cheese over the top. Transfer skillet to the oven and bake until the center is firmly set, approximately 10 to 12 minutes.
Cut omelet in half and slide each half onto an individual plate. Serve immediately.
hints: Walla Walla sweet onion recommend if available.
Jonagold, Gala or McIntosh are the best apple varieties for this recipe.

title: Garlic Herb Vinaigrette Dressing
description: Add a little zip to your kidney-friendly salad with this garlic herb vinaigrette dressing. This homemade dressing tastes better than anything you’ll buy off the shelf and you don’t have to worrying about sodium, phosphorus and potassium.
ingredients: 1 tablespoon Mrs. Dash® original blend herb seasoning
steps: Place all ingredients into a jar with a tight lid and shake.
Ready to serve.
hints: Leftover dressing keeps well in the refrigerator for about 2 weeks.
Use dressing as a marinade for meat or vegetables.

title: High Protein Piña Colada
description: Learn how to make a tasty, high-protein Piña Colada with this easy recipe.
ingredients: 1 ounce Syntrax Nectar Whey Protein Isolate®, Caribbean Cooler
steps: Pour pineapple juice into the blender
Add the protein powder and blend until smooth
Add crushed ice and blend until smooth
Pour into serving glass
Add lemon lime soda or ginger ale
Garnish with small pineapple slices.
hints: Syntrax Nectar Whey Protein Isolate® may be purchased online or at The Vitamin Shoppe. One scoop or individual package equals 1 ounce and provides 23 grams protein.
Freeze the extra serving until ready to drink later.
Use ginger ale (regular or diet) instead of lemon-lime soda if desired.

title: Brunch Nachos
description: Egg and turkey bacon are added to traditional nacho ingredients to create Brunch Nachos, a tasty Mexican dish for your next breakfast or brunch.
ingredients: 4 ounces unsalted large size tortilla chips (about 30 chips)
1 small green bell pepper (or orange, red)
steps: Preheat oven to 375° F. Cut bell pepper into thin strips. Dice red onion. Chop tomatoes and cilantro. Cut turkey bacon into small pieces.
To make pico de gallo, combine chopped tomato, onion and cilantro in a small bowl. Squeeze juice from one lime on top and stir.
To make crema, place sour cream in a bowl and add juice of one lime. Whisk together and refrigerate until ready to serve.
Spray a baking sheet with cooking spray.
Place tortilla chips in one layer on baking sheet. Top chips with dried seasonings, bell pepper and shredded cheese.
Bake in oven for 12 minutes.
While chips are baking, heat a non-stick pan over high heat. Crack eggs into a bowl, whisk and scramble in pan; set aside.
Remove chips from the oven and top with scrambled egg, chopped turkey bacon, pico de gallo, drizzle of crema and additional sprinkle of cilantro. Enjoy!
hints: Elyse chooses Garden of Eatin’® unsalted corn chips.
This nachos recipe is perfect for a breakfast brunch.
For more heat, substitute Monterey jack pepper cheese for cheddar cheese.

title: Jamaican Jerk Chicken
description: Jamaican Jerk Chicken is a Caribbean-style grill-roasted chicken marinated a fiery hot combination of jerk spices and seasonings that include ginger, cloves, allspice, nutmeg, cinnamon, black pepper, hot chilies and a touch of brown sugar for sweetness.
ingredients: 2 habanero or 1 scotch bonnet chili pepper
steps: Coarsely chop the green and yellow onions. Peel and chop the ginger. Mince the garlic cloves. Seed and chop the hot peppers.
Place all ingredients, except chicken, in a food processor and process until smooth.
Place chicken and blended mixture in a dish or large zip-top bag. Seal and refrigerate to marinate for 3 to 24 hours.
Remove chicken from the container and discard remaining marinade.
Heat a grill on medium-high heat. Oil the grill rack, then add chicken and cook on each side for about 10 to 12 minutes. Chicken should reach 165° F before removing from the grill.
hints: Use a grill pan if grill is not available to get char marks on chicken.
If habanera and scotch bonnet peppers are unavailable substitute with your favorite hot chili.

title: Flourless Pumpkin Muffins
description: DaVita dietitian Alissa created a protein-packed pumpkin muffin without flour to share with her dialysis patients. The secret is a combination of peanut butter, eggs and baking soda.
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Line muffin tin with paper liners.
In a medium bowl, combine all ingredients except chocolate chips, mixing until smooth. Fold in chocolate chips.
Distribute batter evenly into 12 muffins.
Bake for 15-18 minutes, until centers are firm and starting to crack. Cool for 15 minutes and enjoy.
hints: If you prefer use reduced-fat peanut butter. This change adds approximately 5 grams of carbohydrate and lowers fat by 3 grams per serving.
These muffins are a tasty way to add extra protein in a snack or meal.
Peanut butter adds more potassium and phosphorus but is a great source of protein. Ask your dietitian if you need to add a phosphate binder when you eat this muffin for a snack.

title: Peach Crisp
description: Juicy Georgia peaches make an irresistible dessert in this kidney-friendly recipe for Peach Crisp. Enjoy it right from the oven when the fruit is warm and the topping extra crisp.
ingredients: 4 cups fresh peaches, peeled, pitted and sliced
steps: Preheat oven to 350º F. Spray a 9” x 9” baking dish with nonstick spray.
Mix peaches with lemon juice and granulated sugar or Splenda® granular sweetener. Pour into baking dish.
Combine flour, oats, brown sugar, nutmeg and cinnamon in a bowl. Cut in margarine with pastry blender or two knives until mixture is crumbly. Sprinkle over peaches.
Bake for 35 to 45 minutes, until fruit is soft and crumbs are brown. Serve warm or at room temperature. Garnish with two tablespoons nondairy whipped topping and a mint leaf.
hints: If fresh peaches are unavailable, use canned or frozen sliced peaches.
2 medium peaches yield approximately 1 cup when peeled and sliced.
If made with Splenda No Calorie Sweetener granular and Splenda brown sugar blend, calories decrease to 247 and 32 g carbohydrate. Count as 2 carbohydrate choices.

title: Chicken Fajitas with Pineapple Salsa
description: Chicken Fajitas with Pineapple Salsa adds a burst of pinapple flavor to a tasty Mexican dish. This spicy meal is a treat for the whole family and recommended on a kidney-friendly diet.
ingredients: 1/2 cup Pineapple Salsa (see recipe under Sauces and Seasonings)
steps: Preheat oven to 300° F. Wrap tortillas in foil; heat in oven for 10 minutes.
Cut chicken breats into 1″ strips.
Place oil in nonstick frying pan over medium heat; add chicken, seasonings and lemon juice. Cook for 3 to 5 minutes.
Add peppers and onion to frying pan; cook for 3 to 5 minutes more or until chicken is no longer pink and juice run clear. Add cilantro to chicken mixture.
Divide chicken mixture between tortillas; fold tortillas over. Serve each with 1 tablespoon of pineapple salsa.
hints: One serving makes a complete meal.
Nutritional information is for 2 fajitas plus 2 tablespoons pineapples salsa.
Adjust the amount of chicken to match your meal plan for a lower or higher protein diet.

title: Tasty Chicken Patties
description: DaVita renal dietitian Melanie from Ohio shares her recipe for kidney-friendly Tasty Chicken Patties, an excellent alternative to salmon or tuna patties for the person who’s following the dialysis diet but doesn’t care for fish.
steps: Set cream cheese out to soften.
Using a fork, mash chicken with juices in a medium bowl.
Add the cream cheese, egg, sage, garlic powder, black pepper, onion powder, Italian seasoning and bread crumbs; mix well.
Form six patties.
In a medium skillet heat olive oil over medium heat.
Fry patties for 5- to 6 minutes on each side or until crispy on the outside and heated through.
hints: Choose the canned chicken lowest in sodium.Melanie uses Keystone Chicken (available at Walmart).
Chicken Patties are very similar to salmon or tuna patties, but might be better liked by someone who doesn’t care for fish.

Look for Kikkoman brand panko bread crumbs– the sodium content is lower compared to commercial and generic unseasoned bread crumbs. Unsalted or low-sodium crushed saltines are an acceptable alternative to the bread crumbs.
Variations: instead of patties, form into 24 chicken meatballs. Meatballs could be eaten as a high-protein snack or used with theDaVita.com Roasted Red Pepper Sauce recipe over pasta.

title: Ginger-Apple Sparkler
description: Ginger-Apple Sparkler is a unique kidney-friendly recipe for your next big party.
ingredients: 1 six-inch piece fresh ginger, finely diced
steps: To prepare ginger syrup, place sugar*, grater ginger and water in a medium saucepan; bring to boil. Reduce heat to low and simmer for 1 hour until ginger flavor is strong. Strain mixture and refrigerate to chill.
To prepare Ginger-Apple Sparkler, place one tablespoon ginger syrup in each glass (use short tumblers).
Fill with ice cubes, pour in 1/2-cup cider and stir to combine.
Garnish with cinnamon stick and crystallized ginger.
hints: Syrup may be stored in the refrigerator up to 2 weeks.
Ginger is often used to help treat nausea and motion sickness.

*For those with diabetes, omit the sugar in ginger syrup. Instead, make concentrated ginger-flavored water. Sweeten to taste with sugar substitute. Nutrients decrease to 61 calories, 15 grams carbohydrate.

title: Bavarian Apple Tart
description: Bavarian Apple Tart is a creamy, cinnamon accented baked treat that will make your kitchen smell as mouthwatering as an Alpine village bakery. DaVita renal dietitian Gertrude from Colorado made a few kidney-friendly modifications and now her fiend’s Bavarian Apple Tart is low in sodium. potassium and phosphorus and suitable for a dialysis diet.
steps: Preheat oven to 450° F.
Set cream cheese out to soften. Peel, core and slice apples.
Cream together butter, 1/3 cup sugar and 1/4 teaspoon vanilla.
Fold in flour to make a dough.
Spread dough on bottom and sides of a 9″ spring form pan.
In a medium bowl combine softened cream cheese and 1/3 cup sugar; mix well.
Add egg and 1/2 teaspoon vanilla; mix until blended.
Pour mixture into pastry-lined pan.
Combine 1/3 cup sugar and cinnamon; toss with apples until all are coated.
Spoon apple mixture over cream cheese layer.
Sprinkle with almonds.
Bake at 450° F for 10 minutes.
Reduce heat to 400° F and continue baking for 25 minutes. Cool.
hints: One medium apple yields 1 cup when peeled and cored.
You can substitute fresh cranberries for slivered almonds on top of tart to reduce phosphorus to 53 mg per serving.
For a lower carbohydrate version diabetics can substitute Splenda® granular instead of sugar; carbohydrate is reduced to 19 grams, calories 266.

title: Chocolate Smoothie
description: Chocolate Smoothie is a creamy treat for people with diabetes who are on dialysis. It features egg whites, which can be a great substitute for other proteins. Try this delicious kidney-friendly recipe today.
steps: Combine cocoa, cold water and sugar.
Stir until sugar dissolves.
Add egg whites and 3 tablespoons of the whipped topping. Mix until whipped topping melts completely.
Top with 1 tablespoon whipped topping and chocolate bar shavings.
hints: Pasteurized egg whites are safe to consume without cooking.
Add 1/4 teaspoon mint extract for a chocolate mint smoothie.
People with diabetes can substitute sugar substitute if desired. Carbohydrate is reduced to 6 grams per serving.

title: Lively Lime Shrimp
description: This kidney-friendly recipe for Lively Lime Shrimp adds a burst of flavor with every bite.
steps: Chop onion and cilantro. Mince chili, garlic and bell pepper. Thinly slice cucumber.
Peel and devein shrimp.
For dressing, stir together lime juice, green onion, cilantro, jalapeno, oil, garlic and salt in a medium bowl.
In a separate medium size bowl, toss shrimp with 2 tablespoons of the dressing to marinade. Reserve remaining dressing. Cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Heat broiler. Remove shrimp from marinade and broil 3-inches from the heat source for 1-1/2 minutes per side or until opaque.
Remove from broiler and immediately toss hot shrimp with reserved dressing and red bell pepper. Cool to room temperature.
Arrange shrimp on cucumber slices and serve.
hints: Barbecue shrimp on a grill instead of broiling if desired.

title: Lemon Flavored Couscous with Zucchini
description: DaVita renal dietitian Martha from Missouri created Lemon Flavored Couscous with Zucchini by adjusting her couscous salad recipe ingredients and adding heat to make a satisfying healthy dish for the kidney diet.
steps: Chop celery, onion and parsley. Quarter and slice zucchini.
In a sauce pan, combine the water and 1 tablespoon of the oil and bring to a boil. Stir in couscous and cover. Remove from heat; let stand 5 minutes.
Combine lemon juice with zest, cayenne pepper and cumin.
In a large skillet, heat remaining 1 tablespoon of canola oil over medium heat and sauté celery, onion and zucchini until softened.
Transfer into a large serving dish and mix together the cooked couscous, the vegetables, cranberries, parsley, lemon juice and seasonings. Fluff with fork before serving. Serve hot.
hints: Mix lemon juice and seasonings together before adding to couscous.
Crookneck squash or other varieties of summer squash can be substituted for zucchini.

title: Frozen Sugar Cookie Sandwiches
description: DaVita renal dietitian, Rachel from Illinois, whipped up a delicious kidney-friendly dessert recipe — Frozen Sugar Cookie Sandwiches. Frosty and sweet whipped topping is sandwiched between two tasty sugar cookies…yum!
ingredients: 1-1/2 cup Splenda® No Calorie granular sweetener
3 cups Reddi-Wip® Fat Free Dairy whipped topping
steps: Preheat oven to 375° F. Set butter and cream cheese out to soften.
In a medium bowl, mix flour, baking soda, and baking powder. Set aside.
In a large bowl, cream together butter and Splenda until smooth. Beat in egg and 1 teaspoon vanilla.
Gradually blend in dry ingredients.
Form teaspoons of dough into balls, and place on ungreased cookie sheet. Flatten the dough ball by pressing down with the bottom of a glass.
Bake 8 to 10 minutes, or until golden. Remove from oven and let stand until completely cool.
With a mixer beat cream cheese, sugar and the remaining vanilla extract. Gently fold in the whipped topping.
Spread cream cheese mixture on half of the cookies, then top each with the remaining cookies to form a sandwich.
Wrap each cookie in foil and place in the freezer for 1 hour or until ready to eat.
hints: Place the cream cheese mixture in a plastic bag, snip off one tip, and pipe the filling onto the cookie.

title: Lemon Blueberry Muffins
description: DaVita dietitian Heather shares one of her family’s favorite recipes, lemon blueberry muffins. She’s modified the recipe to reduce phosphorus and sodium making it kidney-friendly, while maintaining the flavor of comforting, old-fashioned cooking.
ingredients: 1 cup Rice Dream® rice beverage, original (unenriched)
steps: Preheat oven to 375° F.
Combine flour, baking powder and sugar in mixing bowl.
In a separate bowl, combine egg, Rice Dream®, vegetable oil and lemon zest.
Pour liquid ingredients into flour mixture. Mix ingredients lightly until moistened; do not over mix.
Gently fold blueberries into batter.
Lightly spray 12 muffin tins with nonstick cooking spray.
Spoon batter into muffin tins.
Bake for 25 minutes or until toothpick comes out clean.
hints: An alternative to spraying muffin tin with cooking spray is to line tins with muffin paper cups.
Freeze extra muffins then microwave for 30 seconds to serve later.

title: Creamy Vinaigrette Dressing
description: Looking for a dressing that’s thick and delicious? Try the kidney-friendly recipe Creamy Vinaigrette Dressing on the next salad you make.
steps: Mince garlic clove.
Combine all dressing ingredients in a small bowl and mix well.
Pour into a salad dressing flask. Chill until ready to serve.
hints: Use lemon juice instead of lime juice if desired.
Dressing keeps for up to one week in the refrigerator.

title: Basic Dressing
description: Learn how to make a basic, tasty, kidney-friendly dressing that works with almost any salad.
steps: Chop parsley and oregano.
Mix ingredients together to make 1/2 cup basic salad dressing.
hints: Try recipe with basil, dill, rosemary, or tarragon.
Substitute 1 teaspoon dried herbs if fresh herbs are unavailable.
Different flavored oils and vinegars also add variety. Try garlic oil, basil oil, or a small amount of sesame oil. For vinegar, try unseasoned rice vinegar or balsamic vinegar.

title: Citrus Salmon
description: Everyone knows that salmon is one food that’s really good for you. Now DaVita renal dietitian Jennifer from Wisconsin offers up her take on grilled salmon with a fresh lemon dressing spiced with cayenne, Dijon mustard, garlic and capers, plus a touch of basil and dill. Citrus Salmon is an easy-fix entrée that’s tasty and kidney-friendly to boot!
steps: Crush the garlic.
In a small saucepan, combine all the ingredients except the salmon. Heat to a boil, and then reduce the temperature to low and cook for 5 more minutes.

Meanwhile, preheat grill. Place the salmon, skin side down, on a sheet of foil slightly larger than the fish. Fold up the edges so the sauce stays with the salmon on the grill. Place the foil and fish on the grill. Top the salmon with the sauce prepared above.
Cover the grill and cook for 12 minutes or until salmon is cooked. (Do not flip salmon). Cut the salmon into 6 servings.
hints: Recipe was calculated with farmed Atlantic salmon. Wild Alaskan salmon is slightly lower in fat and slightly higher in potassium and phosphorus. Both are acceptable healthy choices for a kidney diet.
You can also cook this recipe in the oven at 350°F for 10 to 15 minutes until done. A good rule of thumb is to allow 10 minutes for each inch of fillet thickness.
If you are on a lower protein diet adjust portion to match your meal plan.

title: Dessert Cups with Fresh Fruit
description: Four kinds of fresh berries, phyllo dough and nondairy whipped topping are the only ingredients in Dessert Cups with Fresh Fruits. Simple, low in phosphorus, potassium and sodium and yummy!
ingredients: 3 cups Cool Whip® frozen dessert topping
steps: Preheat oven to 400° F.
Spray 12-cup muffin pan with butter flavored Pam® cooking spray.
Layer 4 sheets of phyllo dough together, lightly spraying with cooking spray between each layer. Cut phyllo dough into 3-1/2″ squares and place in muffin pan to make dessert cups.
Place muffin pan in oven and bake 10-12 minutes or until phyllo cups are lightly browned. Cool to room temperature.
When ready to serve, fill each phyllo dessert cup with 1/3 cup fresh berries. Top with 1/4 cup Cool Whip dessert topping.
hints: If fresh berries are unavailable, use unsweetened frozen berries instead.
Sweeten fruit with sugar or sugar substitute, if more sweetness is desired.

title: Low Sodium Chicken Soup
description: When you have a craving for a warm and tasty light meal, look no further than the kidney-friendly recipe for Low Sodium Chicken Soup.
ingredients: 1 pound chicken breast, boneless, skinless, cooked
steps: Dice chicken and set aside. Chop onion, celery and parsley; slice carrots 1/2-inch thick.
Sauté butter and onion in a 4-quart pot for 5 minutes, until tender.
Add water and chicken broth and bring to a boil.
Add chicken, celery, parsley and pepper, then cover and simmer for 30 minutes.
Add carrots, cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add frozen vegetables, cover and simmer 20 minutes longer.
hints: Look for reduced sodium broth containing 500 milligrams sodium or less per 1 cup serving. Avoid low sodium broths and bouillons containing potassium chloride—it’s very high in potassium. Recommended brands include Health Valley No Salt, Fat Free Chicken Broth (800-423-4846), Kitchen Basics Natural Chicken Stock and Swanson 50% Less Sodium Chicken Broth.
If you are on hemodialysis or restricted fluid, be sure to count liquid in the soup as part of your fluid allowance for the day.

title: Grill Thyme Corn on the Cob
description: Spice up your next cookout with Grill Thyme Corn on the Cob from DaVita renal dietitian Maria from North Carolina. A combination of thyme, black pepper and a spoon of Parmesan cheese add big flavor and keep sodium low in this summertime favorite!
ingredients: 4 half-ear size frozen corn on the cob
steps: Mix the oil, cheese, thyme and black pepper in a shallow bowl.
Place the corn in the oil mixture and roll to thoroughly coat corn.
Place all four pieces of the corn in the center of a heavy duty aluminum foil sheet. Pour any oil left in the bowl over the corn. Top the corn with 2 ice cubes.
Double fold the top and ends of the foil to make a packet, leaving room for heat to circulate.
Place the foil packet on the grill over medium heat and cook 20 minutes, turning once during cooking.
hints: Compared to most vegetables, corn is higher in phosphorus. A 1/2 ear portion is acceptable for a low phosphorus kidney diet.
Use fresh corn instead of frozen when in season.

title: Easy Egg Salad
description: DaVita dietitian Jennie has patients raving about her Easy Egg Salad recipe, and you are sure to love it too. Try it on a sandwich, on a salad or spread on low-sodium crackers for a high quality protein snack.
ingredients: 1/2 cup sweet onion (Vidalia® or other sweet onion)
1 tablespoon Mrs. Dash® garlic & herb seasoning blend
steps: Hard boil the eggs for 8 minutes; turn the heat off and leave eggs in water for 2 additional minutes.
Peel the eggs and chop or grate to desired consistency.
Finely chop celery and onion. Drain pickle relish then measure 2 tablespoons.
In a medium bowl mix all ingredients together until well blended.
Chill at least 1 hour in the refrigerator before serving.
hints: If eggs are purchased at least a week ahead of time they will be much easier to peel when boiled.
Compare brands and select the mustard, mayonnaise and pickle relish with the lowest sodium content.
Refrigerate overnight for optimal flavor.
Serve with low-sodium crackers or spread on sandwich bread.
Keep egg salad in an insulated bag if taking away from home to keep it cold and avoid food spoilage.

title: German Pancakes
description: If it’s a different kind of pancake you’re craving, look no further than German Pancakes. The DaVita Dietitian Team came together to contribute this comforting breakfast dish for people with kidney disease.
steps: In a medium bowl, combine the flour and sugar. Add the eggs and blend well with a whisk.
Add the milk and vanilla extract. Beat until smooth.

Pour 3 tablespoons of the batter into a heated 8″ or 10″ nonstick skillet, sprayed with nonstick cooking spray. Tilt the pan quickly to spread the batter. Cook until the pancake is brown on underside (about 45 seconds; edges will begin to dry). Flip the pancake and brown the other side. Continue until all the batter is used.
Fold or roll thin pancakes and serve with fruit spread, jam or syrup. If desired, add 1 to 2 tablespoons of ricotta or cream cheese for a filling.
hints: If you have diabetes, use fruit spread or sugar-free syrup as topping.
Nutrient analysis does not include toppings. See chart below for selections.

title: Spaghetti Squash Stir-fry
description: Most varieties of winter squash are high in potassium. Spaghetti squash is one exception with only 180 mg potassium in one cup. But how do you prepare it? DaVita dietitian Susan shared her Spaghetti Squash Stir-fry recipe. It’s sure to be a hit with the whole family.
ingredients: 14 ounce bag classic slaw mixture with carrots
steps: Slice celery diagonally and dice onion. Set aside.

Wash spaghetti squash and pierce with a fork several times around the squash. Microwave on high for 2 minutes to soften. Cut the stem end off, cut in half lengthwise and scoop out seeds with membrane.
Place squash halves cut side down in a microwave safe dish. Put plastic wrap over the top with one corner vented. Microwave on high for 12 minutes. Cool and scoop out with a fork. Set aside.
Whisk together soy sauce, water, garlic, brown sugar, ginger paste, pepper. Set aside.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add celery and onion, and cook until tender, approximately 3-4 minutes.
Add cabbage mix and stir until heated through, approximately 2-3 minutes.
Stir in spaghetti squash and soy sauce mixture until well combined, approximately 2 minute.
Serve immediately!
hints: If desired use 2 teaspoons fresh grated ginger instead of ginger paste.
Adjust portion to 1/2 cup for a lower potassium meal.

title: Sheet Pan Brussel Sprouts and Pears
description: Seasoned Cabbage Steaks add a new twist to this high-antioxidant cruciferous vegetable. Only 5 ingredients, and all you have to do is slice, season and bake.
steps: Preheat the oven to 400° F.
Remove the outside leaves of the Brussels sprouts. Cut in half. Cut the pears into 1/2-inch cubes.
Place 1 teaspoon olive oil in a mixing bowl. Add Brussels sprouts and toss to coat with the oil.
Transfer Brussels sprouts to a 9” x 13” pan and spread into a single layer on half of the pan. Bake for 12 minutes.
Place the remaining teaspoon olive oil in the mixing bowl. Add pears and toss to coat with oil.
Remove Brussels sprouts from the oven and add the pears to the other half of the pan. Roast for an additional 12 minutes, or until pears are tender.
Drizzle pears with 1 teaspoon balsamic vinegar glaze. Mix sprouts and pears together in a serving bowl.
hints: Balsamic vinegar glaze, also called balsamic vinegar reduction, may be purchased or made at home. For homemade, using a small saucepan bring 1 cup of vinegar to a boil then reduce to medium heat. Cook for 10 to 15 minutes until vinegar is reduced by half or until it reaches your desired consistency. Store extra in a covered container in the refrigerator.

title: Jellied Cranberry Sauce
description: Jellied Cranberry Sauce is a great reminder that you don’t have to wait for Thanksgiving to accent a dish with kidney-friendly cranberry sauce.
steps: In a medium saucepan combine sugar and 1 cup water; bring to a boil.
Add cranberries to water and return to a boil. Reduce the heat to medium and boil for 10 minutes while stirring occasionally.
Pour cooked cranberries into a wire mesh strainer over a mixing bowl. Using the back of a spoon mash berries to force pulp into the bowl. Discard skins.
Stir sauce and pour into a serving bowl. Cool at room temperature, then chill in the refrigerator until ready to serve.
hints: For a low sugar version use Splenda or other sugar-free sweetener.
Use frozen cranberries if fresh are not available.

title: Air Fryer Bagel Big Bites
description: This fun dish may bring a smile to your face. Serve with a greed salad and enjoy!
steps: Turn air fryer to 400 degrees F.
Arrange bagel thins cut side up, 4 thins total.
Dice the bell pepper into small pieces. Distribute marinara sauce amongst the bagel thins.
Distribute cheeses and pepper equally to bagel thins.
Bake in air fryer for 4-5 minutes.
hints: Can also be made in a regular oven at the same temperature, but increase the time to 10 minutes.
To make this gluten-free, Elyse used the brand O’Doughs Gluten Free Bagel Thins® (no phosphorus additives).
This recipe is a bit higher in sodium, so balance out your meals for the day. Look for bagel thins with the lowest amount of sodium per serving.
Use different colored bell pepper to change up the recipe.

title: Grilled Chicken Pesto Pizza
description: Pizza and chicken are two of the most popular dinner items. Now you can combine both with DaVita dietitian Amie’s kidney-friendly recipe for Grilled Chicken Pesto Pizza. Sun-dried tomato pesto combined with sautéed sweet peppers and onion replace the traditional red pizza sauce.
steps: Dice the bell peppers, onion and chives. Chop or shred the chicken.
Heat a tablespoon of olive oil and sauté the diced peppers and onion. Add the tomato pesto and cook for 2 minutes. Set aside for later.
